topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture structure, learning outcomes, and framework for understanding the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and mutational activation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt signaling cascades drive growth signal autonomy and bypass growth inhibition.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how differentiation blocks arrest cells in immature, proliferative states across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the mechanisms by which cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through deregulation of p53 and Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and cellular stress surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality by overcoming telomere shortening and how stress signals converge on p53 genome surveillance.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolite signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanisms of cancer metabolic rewiring, including aerobic glycolysis, Krebs cycle alterations, and oncometabolite signaling.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and vascularization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch required for tumors to establish new blood vessels and prevent hypoxia-induced necrosis.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the progression of cancer metastasis from local invasion and circulation to metastatic colonization and its genomic characteristics.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing the convergence of cancer hallmarks and providing closing remarks.
